title: PGI posted but COGS is unexpected
prompt: A customer delivery has posted goods issue successfully, but Finance says the COGS or inventory posting is wrong. Explain how you diagnose the issue and which exceptions can change the simple PGI-to-COGS pattern.
expected_points: Start from the delivery, material, quantity and PGI accounting document rather than the G/L account alone.
Confirm material valuation and account-determination context before changing financial mappings.
Check COGS split if the total cost is correct but component accounts differ.
Separate the typical PGI baseline of COGS versus inventory from specialized recognition or valuated-stock-in-transit scenarios.
Prove whether the first wrong state is logistics quantity, valuation, account determination, or recognition timing.
follow_up_questions: What if total COGS is correct but the split accounts are wrong?
When can a sales goods issue fail to create COGS at the moment you expect?
red_flags: Assumes every PGI always has identical accounting timing
Changes the G/L manually before checking valuation and source event
Treats COGS and revenue recognition as the same decision

title: Correct GR quantity, wrong inventory value
prompt: A purchase-order goods receipt has the correct physical quantity, but the inventory value and price variance surprise the business. Build a diagnosis that separates logistics quantity from valuation and accounting.
expected_points: Confirm PO price, received quantity and account-assignment context.
Identify material price control and relevant valuation context before interpreting the stock value.
Explain that standard-price and moving-average-price behavior can create different stock and price-difference effects.
Check whether invoice receipt occurred before the goods receipt because sequence can affect the valuation basis.
Trace the accounting document and automatic account-determination inputs rather than treating the material document as full financial proof.
follow_up_questions: How does an account-assigned purchase order change the receiving side of the posting?
What would you inspect if the price difference is correct but posts to the wrong G/L?
red_flags: Says correct quantity proves correct value
Edits the PO price after posting without understanding document/reversal consequences

title: GR IR balance after procurement completion
prompt: The warehouse says all goods are received and Accounts Payable says all supplier invoices are posted, but the GR/IR account still has a material balance. Explain how you decide whether it is a timing difference, data problem, or accounting exception.
expected_points: Use PO history to compare received and invoiced quantity and value at item level.
Check missing or reversed GR/IR documents, price differences, delivery costs and invoice/receipt sequence.
Distinguish a legitimate still-open business event from an old residual that requires reconciliation action.
Do not clear GR/IR manually until you prove that no further receipt or invoice should arrive.
Connect procurement, warehouse, supplier and Finance ownership because GR/IR reconciliation is cross-functional.
follow_up_questions: What if received quantity is greater than invoiced quantity?
How can delivery costs create or distort a GR/IR exception?
red_flags: Looks only at the G/L balance without PO history
Assumes every open GR/IR item is an accounting configuration defect

title: Billing amount correct, revenue account wrong
prompt: The customer invoice amount and tax are correct, but the revenue G/L account is wrong. Trace the ownership from Sales Billing into Finance without using pricing as a repair mechanism.
expected_points: Confirm commercial billing values and FI posting status first.
Identify the pricing account key but keep commercial calculation separate from revenue account determination.
Trace chart of accounts, sales organization, customer and material account-assignment groups and other relevant billing/account inputs.
Prove which account-determination input selected the wrong G/L and correct the owning configuration or master data.
Explain that Billing owns the commercial document while Finance owns the posted accounting state after the handoff.
follow_up_questions: What changes if no accounting document was created at all?
Who should own a wrong customer account-assignment group versus a wrong G/L mapping?
red_flags: Says the issue is purely FI because the invoice already exists
Stops without checking the account key and master-data inputs

title: Production complete but order balance remains
prompt: A production order is technically complete and the finished product was received, but the order still carries a financial balance. Explain the cost-flow diagnosis before anyone posts a manual journal.
expected_points: Check component issues, activity/actual cost postings and finished-goods receipt value.
Compare production-order actual debits with output credits and identify variance or missing posting.
Check order status, settlement rule and receiver such as material or sales-order context.
Separate an operationally complete order from a financially settled order and consider legitimate period/WIP timing.
Use settlement and variance evidence before proposing a direct FI correction.
follow_up_questions: What if the finished-goods receipt is missing rather than settlement?
How does a sales-order receiver change the boundary?
red_flags: Posts the remaining balance directly to a G/L
Assumes TECO automatically means zero financial balance

title: Freight charges and carrier invoice do not reconcile
prompt: Transportation Management shows the expected carrier charges, but the carrier invoice cannot be reconciled in MM and Finance. Trace the freight settlement chain and identify where the first wrong value or state can appear.
expected_points: Start from freight order or booking charge calculation and confirm the Freight Settlement Document state.
Trace creation and acceptance of the MM service purchase order and service entry sheet or equivalent follow-on documents.
Check the financial accrual/cost posting and cost-allocation context rather than assuming TM completion equals financial completion.
Compare carrier invoice verification against the MM follow-on values and explain quantity/value variance or missing documents.
Include cancellation/reversal propagation because correction spans TM, MM and FI.
follow_up_questions: What if the FSD was cancelled after the service entry sheet was created?
How can inbound versus outbound freight allocation change the financial destination?
red_flags: Stops at the freight order because charges look correct
Edits the carrier invoice to match TM without checking MM follow-on documents
Treats FSD posting as the final financial state
